title.narrative: Enhanced Public Sector Efficiency Technical Assistance Loan

description.narrative: The objective of the Enhanced Public Sector Efficiency Technical Assistance Project for Panama is to assist public agencies of the borrower in producing, using and disseminating timely and quality performance information, thereby allowing a more efficient, transparent and account use of the Borrower's public budget funds. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening performance-based budget management and evaluation. The provision of support to the Ministry of Finance (MEF), including, goods, Information and Technology (IT) equipment, operating costs, training and technical assistance for the carrying out of activities aimed at improving the institutional and technical capacities of MEF for performance-based strategic planning and budgeting in order to create conditions for enhancing the quality of public spending. The second component is the new financial management model: strengthening budget execution, treasury, accounting and control. The third component is the strengthening public procurement and contracting. The provision of support to the General Directorate of Public Procurement (DGCP), including goods and IT equipment, training and technical assistance, for the reform of the Borrower's public procurement process, through the carrying out of activities aimed at supporting the institutional strengthening of DGCP, as well as building the capacity of public procurement officials. Finally, the fourth component is the creation and support of project management capacities.

The objective of the Project is to assist public agencies of the Borrower in producing, using and disseminating timely and quality performance information, thereby allowing a more efficient, transparent and accountable use of the Borrower#s public budget funds.

title.narrative: Increased institutional coverage of the new ISTMO model in Central Government
Improved performance orientation of the budget

baseline.value: The budget document does not use program classifications with very limited financial performance information

actual.value: Target has been achieved. In 2018, DIPRENA selected 6 new entities to pilot performance budgeting in parallel with the regular budget submission process.

title.narrative: Extended functional coverage of the new ISTMO model

baseline.value: The current SIAFPA does not include functionalities for budget preparation and is not harmonized with national payroll, procurementand public investment system

actual.value: Achieved. ISTMO includes all functions and integration with National Debt (SIGADE), Single Treasury Account, and Tax. The only integration missing is that with PanamaCompra 3 and public investment (not part of end target). In addition, ISTMO has implemented integration with payroll (EPD) and SIAFPA Consolidado.

title.narrative: Increased institutional coverage of the new ISTMO model in Decentralized Government

comment.narrative: <p><strong>The new PFM system (ISTMO) was rolled out to all Central Government entities in 2016. However, MEF continued to face difficulties with the quality, comparability and reliability of financial information produced by ISTMO notably: significant inconsistencies in accounting information transferred from old PFM system to the initial balances under the ISTMO;  unreconciled payroll and treasury data and financial information on state fixed assets;  and inability to post tax and non-tax revenues in ISTMO. Inorder to publish consolidated financial statements, MEF will need to lower material inconsistencies to a non-significant level. In November 2020, MEF issued a Ministerial Resolution that mandates procedures to guarantee the publication of Central Government consolidated financial statements, including through the reduction of accounting inconsistencies by: clearing of initial balances of ISTMO; reconciling inconsistencies on the operations of the Single Treasury Account (STA); and including additional financial information on state fixed assets (property, plant and equipment), tax and non-tax revenues. MEF’s Institutional Plan, as mandated by the Ministerial Decree, establishes the intragovernmental procedures and responsibilities that guarantee the production and publication of consolidated financial statements of the Central Government. The issuance of the Ministerial Decree is a prior action in a proposed World Bank Development Policy Operation. With the implementation of the Institutional Plan, this target is expected to be achieved by end of 2021. </strong></p>

title.narrative: Quality of public sector financial information improved

baseline.value: Financial reports do not provide complete information on government revenue and expenditures thus impeding the monitoring of budgetexecution

actual.value: Partly achieved. ISTMO deployed in 100 percent of Central Government and 89 percent of decentralized agencies.

title.narrative: Public entities increase the production and dissemination of performance information linked with budget information

baseline.value: Performance information is limited, not publicly available and not linked to financial information

actual.value: Not achieved. The project supported the development and design of performance metrics for the 2018 budget, which, however, were notapplied. The budget still applies a basic program classification at agency level but it does not apply a systematic approach to program definition or include performance indicators.

title.narrative: Increased use of ISTMO in Decentralized Government

baseline.value: SIAFPA, RAMAN, and all the previous information systems which supported the budget execution, were basically ex-post registry systems. Implementation of ex-ante controls was not feasible

actual.value: Target is achieved. 75% of Decentralized Entities´ budget is subject to ITSMOs controls and regulation (excluding transfers, fondos financieros, and payroll)

title.narrative: Increased use of ISTMO in Central Government

baseline.value: SIAFPA, RAMAN, and all the previous information systems which supported the budget execution, were basically ex-post registry systems. Implementation of ex-ante controls was not feasible

actual.value: Target is achieved. 99.98% of Central Governments Budget is subject to ITSMOs controls and regulation (excluding transfers, fondos financieros and payroll)

baseline.value: The current PanamaCompra system has no instruments to facilitate complaints about procurement processes

actual.value: Panama Compra 3 Platform includes functionalities for managing complaints. Implementation of the Platform has been initiated in July 2018 and is expected to be completed by July 2021.

baseline.value: Update of Law 22 (2006) and regulation 366 (2006). The law has changed 6 times between 2009 and 2014, but the regulation 366 has never been modified.

actual.value: Target has been achieved. Law 61, reforming public contracting in Panama, published September 27, 2017 in the Official Gazette (reforms the text of Law 22 of 2006). Executive Decree (Regulation) 40, published April 10, 2018 in the Official Gazette (replaces Regulation 366 of 2006).

baseline.value: 60% competitive procurement processes of Central and Decentralized Government are publicly and daily available through PanamaCompra2

actual.value: Partly achieved. PanamaCompra 3 designed and tested. New regulatory framework in place.
